This operation can be performed in two ways: through a Catenary Anchor Leg Mooring (CALM) buoy or directly from the FPSO, which is known as tandem

offloading. The CALM buoy is a floating structure anchored to the seabed and connected to the FPSO by submarine hoses (see Figure 1-5). Its facilities include a hawser, which is generally a nylon rope, to which the tanker can moor, and a string of floating hoses that connects to the tanker’s midship manifold through which the oil will be transferred.
